findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded into the Lambda function's environment variables and therefore stored in the Terraform state and source repository. Anyone with read access to the code, state file, or the Lambda console can retrieve and reuse these static credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key, allowing any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration to read the plaintext secrets without a separate KMS grant.
The function does not specify code_signing_config_arn, so unsigned deployment packages can be pushed to the function, permitting tampered code to execute with the function's IAM role.
The nodejs12.x runtime is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the function exposed to known unpatched vulnerabilities in the runtime environment.
